operations.description:
Creates a membership type at the chain level. Membership types define reusable packages
(e.g., "10 visits", "Monthly unlimited") that can be sold at the chain's Locations.
Omitted optional fields take their defaults.

**Covered services.** At least one service or service category is required. Which fields
the backend reads depends on whether the chain has the unlimited memberships feature:
- Without it: `services` and `service_categories`, objects that map an ID to a number of visits,
  e.g. `{"13160808": 5}`.
- With it: `service_links`, an array of `{service_id, service_category_id, is_unlimited, count}` items.

The form that does not match the chain is silently ignored. A request that sends both
`service_links` and `services` or `service_categories` is rejected with `422`.

**Note:** Requires chain-level permissions.

operations.description:
Replaces the settings of a membership type. Send the full type: omitted optional fields
are reset to their defaults. The request body and the covered-services rules are the same
as in Create membership type.
An archived type cannot be updated (`422`); unarchive it first.

**After the first membership of the type is sold**, the request still succeeds, but the
backend silently keeps the current `cost`, `period`, `period_unit_id`, `expiration_type_id`,
`is_allow_empty_code`, the balance model (`is_united_balance`, `is_united_balance_unlimited`,
`united_balance_services_count`), `category`, `availability` and the covered services.
Only a type with a shared balance can gain services or categories: the ones sent are added
to the type and to the memberships already sold; none are removed.
Compare the response with the request to see what was kept.

**Note:** Requires chain-level permissions.

Fully updates an Appointment. This is not a partial update: for a standard Appointment,
resend `staff_id`, `services`, `client`, `datetime`, and `seance_length`, including when
only `custom_fields` needs to change. A missing required field returns `422`.

For a Group Event Appointment, send `activity_id` and `client`. The `activity_id` must
match the Appointment's current Group Event. The API obtains `staff_id`, `services`,
`datetime`, and `seance_length` from that Group Event.

### Updating only custom fields

1. Get the current Appointment.
2. Copy the required main fields into this request without changing them.
3. Add the new values to `custom_fields`, using each configured field code as a key.

`custom_fields_record_values_edit_access`. Without both permissions, custom Appointment
Field values are not updated.

The request can be rejected when the Appointment is waiting for online payment, lies
outside the Business User's allowed editing period, is fully paid, or has an arrived
client and the Business User lacks the corresponding edit permission.

If `is_sale_bill_printed` is `true`, keep the resent date, time, client, attendance status,
Team Member, and Services unchanged when updating only custom fields. Changes covered by
the printed receipt can require reversing the receipt first.

operations.description:
Change the attendance status of one Appointment without resending the full
Appointment. The body field is `attendance` (not `visit_attendance`). The
supported statuses are `-1` (did not come), `0` (waiting), `1` (came), and
`2` (confirmed). Read the current status from the Appointment first.

The Business User needs `record_form_access` and `edit_records_access` for
this Location. The Appointment must fall within the Location's
`records_edit_last_days_count` editing window (`-1` means no history limit).
A request can also be rejected while online payment is pending, by payment
policy, or when a printed sale receipt would be invalidated. With a printed
receipt, only `1` and `2` remain eligible statuses. Submitting the current
status leaves it unchanged.

Appointments linked into one visit share an attendance group. Changing one
Appointment can update the status of other Appointments in that visit and
trigger related payment, loyalty, and notification processing. The `records`
response field contains timetable change data; it is not a per-ID bulk result.

For a bounded bulk workflow, select a finite set of Appointment IDs, read
each Appointment and confirm its Location, current status, and visit link,
then send one request per distinct attendance group. Re-read affected
Appointments after each change, record successes and failures per group, and
stop or report on a failed request. This endpoint offers no atomic bulk
operation or all-or-nothing rollback.

Cancels an appointment as a command: the response is the appointment with
`status: "cancelled"` and `cancelled_at` set. Optionally stores a `reason` and
whether to notify the client.

Requires `Idempotency-Key`. Cancelling an already cancelled appointment with the same
key is a no-op returning the same result.

A cancelled appointment stays readable: `getAppointment` returns it with
`status: "cancelled"` rather than `404`, and `listAppointments` keeps returning it, so a
client synchronising the journal sees the cancellation instead of silently losing the row.
Filter on the `status` field to hide them. In a visit built from several appointments,
cancelling one does not cancel the visit: the remaining appointments and any payments
already recorded stay, and `amount_to_pay_minor` is recomputed when the visit is read.

operations.description:
Looks up a gift card or membership by its number and reports whether it can pay the visit
resolved from `appointment_id`.

This is for instruments the client does not hold in Altegio: a gift card received as a
present, or a membership bought at another location of the chain. Instruments already
attached to the client come back from `getVisit` in `payment_methods` and need no search.
Results carry the same applicability fields, so both are passed to `createPayment` the
same way.

client-visible outcome — empty result or `422 instrument_not_applicable` — and never distinct
codes that would reveal whether a number exists elsewhere. This search and number-bearing
`createPayment` attempts share a per-credential, per-Location rate limit (`429` +
`Retry-After`).

operations.description:
OAuth 2.0 token endpoint (RFC 6749). Supports three grants:

- `authorization_code` — exchange a code obtained from the browser
  `GET /oauth/authorize` flow (PKCE `code_verifier` required). Returns an access
  token and a rotating refresh token.
- `client_credentials` — machine-to-machine token for a marketplace installation.
  Always requires the explicit `location_id`; the installation is resolved from the
  authenticated OAuth client plus that Location. No refresh token is returned.
- `refresh_token` — rotate a refresh token from the Authorization Code flow.
  The previous refresh token is invalidated; replaying it revokes the token family.

Confidential clients authenticate with HTTP Basic (`client_secret_basic`); public
clients (PKCE-only) send their `client_id` in the form body. There is **no password
grant**.

Errors from this endpoint use the standard OAuth 2.0 error object
(`{"error": "...", "error_description": "..."}`), not `application/problem+json`.
